entities.label: Institution
entities.summary:
Masjid Al-Muttaqin (مسجد المتقين, 'Mosque of the God-Fearing/Pious') is a mosque in Singapore — serving the Malay Muslim community within MUIS's comprehensive framework. The name 'Al-Muttaqin' (Arabic: المتقين, 'the pious,' 'the god-fearing') refers to the Islamic concept of taqwa — God-consciousness, piety, and fear of God — considered one of the highest virtues in Islam and the Quran's most frequently cited criterion for spiritual excellence (the Quran states that 'the most honored of you in the sight of God is the most righteous among you,' 49:13).

Singapore's mosque naming conventions collectively create a theological landscape encoding Islamic virtues: Al-Furqan (discernment), Al-Ghufran (divine forgiveness), Al-Huda (divine guidance), Al-Istiqamah (steadfastness), Al-Khair (goodness), Al-Mawaddah (affection), Al-Mukminin (believers), Al-Muttaqin (the pious) — together representing a comprehensive Islamic moral vocabulary embedded in the city's religious architecture. This practice reflects Islamic civilization's tradition of naming religious institutions to encode theological aspirations.

The mosque serves the full range of Islamic community needs: the five daily prayers, Friday khutbah (sermon), Ramadan tarawih prayers and iftar gatherings, Eid prayer celebrations, Islamic education (fardhu ain — the basic religious obligations), and social services including zakat distribution and family counseling. Singapore's MUIS coordinates all these services across the mosque network, ensuring quality and consistency in religious programming.
